clue.text: Curious-a penny for a piece of steak

parts.note: rum is an old British word for strange or curious
P is the standard abbreviation for a penny in British money

explanation.surface: Someone finds it odd that a slice of steak should cost only a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen after 'Curious' is a printing quirk; 'a' is just a link. RUMP is a cut of beef from the hindquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rump is a named cut of beef taken from the animal's hindquarters, sold as steak.

clue.text: Spots the cane coming out

indicators.note: coming out suggests the letters of the word cane emerge in a new order

explanation.surface: A schoolboy's pimples appear when the cane comes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out' rearranges CANE; 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is the skin condition marked by pimples, so spots name it by its symptom.

clue.text: Bank of Scotland

parts.note: not the financial institution but a grassy slope as the Scots call it

explanation.walkthrough: The Bank of Scotland is a famous Scottish bank; here 'bank' means a hillside, and the Scots word for it is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect a brae is a hillside or steep slope, a bank of earth.

clue.text: Officer uninterested in detail?

explanation.surface: A senior army man who cannot be bothered with the small print.
explanation.definitionFit: A general is a high-ranking army officer; general also means broad, not specific or detailed.

clue.text: Receive applause, but think again

parts.note: to reap is to receive or gather in, as a reward
praise is approval, the sense applause carries

explanation.surface: A performer is cheered but has second thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappraise is to assess anew, reconsidering a judgement already made.

clue.text: Curt censor resolved to skimp work

indicators.note: resolved here means solved again or broken down, so the letters of curt censor are rearranged

explanation.surface: A brusque official is determined to do slapdash work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' looks like 'determined' but signals the rearrangement of CURT CENSOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut corners is an idiom for doing a job cheaply or hastily, skipping proper steps.

clue.text: Youth's spell as a vegetarian?

parts.note: a period of eating only greens, read as the time of one's youthful inexperience

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra: 'my salad days, when I was green in judgment'.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad days is an idiom for the carefree, inexperienced period of one's youth.

clue.text: Gosh it's hard to fit into seat in church

indicators.note: to fit into says the hard letter goes inside the church seat

parts.note: a pew is a bench seat in a church
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone remarks how difficult it is to squeeze into a church bench.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise or relief, interchangeable as interjections.

clue.text: A price apt to be changed for each person

indicators.note: to be changed says the letters of a price apt are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper says a fitting price ought to be revised for every customer.
explanation.definitionFit: Per capita is Latin for 'by heads', used in English to mean per individual.

clue.text: Gradually bit the food

parts.note: a piece is a bit or portion
a meal is a serving of food

explanation.surface: Someone slowly bit into their dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit' reads as a verb (past of bite) but is a noun meaning a portion; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Piecemeal describes doing something a little at a time, step by step.

clue.text: Motorists needing a lift -in this?

parts.note: drivers wanting a ride would want to be given one in a vehicle, and a garage hoist lifts one

explanation.walkthrough: A motorist's vehicle may need a lift (a hoist) at the garage, while a hitchhiker needing a lift wants a ride in one.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is the road vehicle motorists drive, and the one a lift is given in.

clue.text: Knocks a piece of wood about

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the piece of wood round, reading its letters backwards

parts.note: a spar is a pole or length of timber, as on a ship

explanation.surface: Someone taps a bit of timber around.
explanation.definitionFit: Raps are sharp blows or taps, the noise a fist makes on a door.

clue.text: Home of Joan, a Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: Joan's birthplace, belonging to a Catholic woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Joan of Arc, the French saint, is named as if Arc were her home town, a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan of Arc takes her name as if from a place, so this jokingly names where she is from.

clue.text: Wonderful directors, just right for shipping

parts.note: star as an adjective means outstanding or wonderful
a board is the body of directors of a company

explanation.surface: An excellent company board is perfect for running a shipping line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shipping' reads as a business but points to vessels: starboard is the right side of a ship. 'just' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Starboard is the nautical term for the right-hand side of a vessel facing forward.

clue.text: Contaminant found in all meals? No!

indicators.note: found here means cast or forge anew, so the letters of all meals and no are melted down and reshaped

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether a contaminant is present in all meals, and is told no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' looks like 'discovered' but means to cast metal, so ALL MEALS plus NO is reshaped; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Salmonella bacteria contaminate food and cause poisoning, a classic kitchen contaminant.

clue.text: Notice embassy entrance

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
a diplomatic mission is an embassy

explanation.surface: A sign is posted at the door of a foreign embassy.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission means entry, the act of being let in.

clue.text: Huge bird gives amusement at fair

parts.note: big means huge or large
a dipper is a small bird of fast streams

explanation.surface: A giant bird provides entertainment at a funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a BIG DIPPER is a roller coaster at a fairground; 'gives' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A big dipper is the British name for a roller coaster ride at a funfair.

clue.text: Right in a strange way? Wrong

indicators.note: in places the right letter inside the jumbled word
strange suggests the word way is made odd by rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether being right in an odd way is really wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges WAY to AWY, and 'in' puts R inside it; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Awry means amiss or off course, as plans go wrong.

clue.text: Robin's coat?

parts.note: the bird's covering rather than a garment worn by someone named Robin

explanation.definitionFit: A bird's feathers form its covering, the robin's being its red-breasted outfit.

clue.text: A large part of the earth is peaceful

definitions.text: A large part of the earth

explanation.surface: A big region of the globe is calm.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific is the largest ocean, covering a third of the globe; pacific also means calm and peace-loving.

clue.text: Staying on the move in such darkness

definitions.note: adjective sense: the definition describes the kind of darkness meant

indicators.note: on the move says the letters of staying shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone keeps moving about in pitch blackness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such darkness' points to the adjective: Stygian gloom is darkness like that of the Styx, the river of the Greek underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Stygian, from the underworld river Styx, describes extremely gloomy, pitch-black conditions.

clue.text: Throw on to the ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship before a vessel's name

explanation.surface: Someone flings something onto the vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' and 'the' are links; SS is the steamship prefix.
explanation.definitionFit: To toss is to throw lightly, like a coin.

clue.text: One would be unwilling to die like this

definitions.text: One would be unwilling to die like this

parts.words: One would be unwilling to die like this
parts.note: unwilling read as having no will, describing someone who dies without a legal will

explanation.definitionFit: Dying intestate means dying without having made a valid will.

clue.text: Not over weight

indicators.note: over says the word not is turned over, reading backwards

explanation.surface: A claim of being underweight rather than overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: A ton is a unit of weight, 2,240 pounds in Britain.

clue.text: Something to quieten one, so quiet

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: Something meant to calm a person down is fittingly hushed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sop is a concession given to pacify or placate someone.

clue.text: There's still one mystery in the mountains

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'not yet'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single unsolved puzzle lingers among the peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's' is a link. The yeti is the abominable snowman of Himalayan legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti is a legendary unexplained creature said to roam the Himalayas.

clue.text: Display for a long time in food store

indicators.note: in says the long time sits inside the food store

parts.note: a pantry is a cupboard or room where food is kept
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: An exhibit lasts ages in a grocery shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Pageantry is elaborate ceremonial show and spectacle.

clue.text: Not all NATO partners are at the summit

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Only some alliance members hold top positions.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'are at the summit' reads loosely as 'on top', the sense of the answer as a predicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Atop means on the top of, so being atop is being at the summit.

clue.text: Side of cooked meat

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of meat are tampered with, rearranged

explanation.surface: A side dish of prepared meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' looks like a side dish but means a sports side; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A side in sport is a group of players, a squad.

clue.text: Shortly you will scream

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

indicators.note: shortly means the word will is cut down to its contracted form, as in a written apostrophe

parts.note: will taken in its contracted form 'll

explanation.surface: A warning that you are about to shriek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' shortens 'you will' to the dialect contraction YE'LL.
explanation.definitionFit: To yell is to shout loudly, a cry like a scream.

clue.text: Scottish relatives keep money in container

indicators.note: keep means the container holds the money inside it

parts.note: a can is a tin container
L stands for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Scottish kinsfolk hoard their cash in a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is a Scottish kinship group sharing a surname and ancestry.

clue.text: Treacherous, executed — that's fair

indicators.note: executed means beheaded, so the word for treacherous loses its first letter

parts.note: treasonable means guilty of treason, treacherous

explanation.surface: A traitor is put to death, and someone says that is just.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' signals beheading: TREASONABLE loses its head, T.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasonable means fair and sensible, within reason.
